label: Linear Equations in One Variable
overview: A linear equation in one variable has exactly one unknown and can always be solved by isolating that variable through inverse operations. SAT questions range from straightforward one-step equations to multi-step equations with fractions, parentheses, or variables on both sides. Every question reduces to the same goal: get x alone on one side.

conceptDiagram.caption: Solving strategy: simplify both sides, then move variables left and constants right

keyFormulas.name: Variables on both sides
keyFormulas.latex: ax + b = cx + d \implies (a-c)x = d - b \implies x = \dfrac{d-b}{a-c}

steps.title: Collect variable terms on one side
Isolate x
steps.content: Add 3 to both sides, then divide by 3.

commonMistakes.fix: Multiply every term inside the parentheses. With a negative outside, all signs flip: −3(x−2) = −3x + 6.

commonMistakes.mistake: Performing the operation on only one side
commonMistakes.fix: Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other. Writing each step as a complete equation helps.

quickTip: Always check your answer: substitute back into the original equation and verify both sides are equal.
